name: Material Design 3 / Material 3 Expressive
origin: Google introduced Material Design in 2014 as an answer to the loss of affordance in pure flat design: surfaces are virtual paper with a height in dp, and shadows make that height visible. In 2021, Material You (M3) brought the real systemic break - color is no longer picked but computed from a seed color in the perceptual HCT model into tonal palettes, from which more than 30 semantic color roles are derived; on Android that seed can come from the user's wallpaper (Dynamic Color). At Google I/O in May 2025, Google added Material 3 Expressive, backed by 46 studies with more than 18,000 participants: 35 new shapes with shape morphing, a spring-based motion system in place of duration-plus-bezier, emphasized type styles, and new components such as button groups, FAB menu, split button and loading indicator. The line shipped from September 2025 with Android 16 QPR1.
idea: A single seed color generates the entire color system algorithmically, and depth comes not from shadows but from higher surfaces moving tonally closer to the accent color. Expressive adds a second layer to that: shape and motion carry meaning, not just color.
markers: Shape scale with fixed steps: xs 4px / s 8px / m 12px / l 16px / xl 28px / full
Grouped lists with 28px outer and 4px inner corners at a 3px gap
Elevation through tonal surfaces instead of shadows: surface / container-low #F7F2FA / container #F3EDF7 / container-high #ECE6F0 / container-highest #E6E0E9
State layer as an overlay of the on-color: 8% on hover, 10-12% on active, 12% on focus
Use intended color-role pairs: primary/on-primary and primary-container/on-primary-container; check contrast after changing values or states
Tonal palette in tone steps 10/20/30/40/80/90/95 - fills come from tone 90, text on them from tone 10
Filled icon variants (fill, no stroke) on a 24px grid in tonal containers; 48dp hit area, Expressive buttons up to 56px tall
Spring motion instead of bezier: stiffness/damping/initial velocity, with visible overshoot
Shape morphing as a state signal: the pill becomes a squircle when pressed (999px to 12px)

params.radius: 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 28 / full - and in Expressive animated between those steps
params.density: medium to airy - large radii and 48dp targets force air
params.depth: tonal: every level is its own surface-container step. Shadows only on the FAB and floating elements
params.color: A seed color generates five core tonal palettes through HCT: primary, secondary, tertiary, neutral and neutral variant. Semantic color roles draw from these palettes; error has a separate palette.
params.type: Roboto Flex as a variable font, five roles (display/headline/title/body/label) in three sizes each, plus 15 emphasized cuts for accent moments
params.motion: spring-based, not bezier: the Expressive scheme with visible overshoot, around 300-550ms perceived duration, standard on 21 components in Compose
params.texture: none - surfaces are pure tonal values

examples.name: Android 16 system UI (2025)
examples.what: quick settings as grouped tiles with 28px outer and 4px inner corners, buttons that morph from pill to squircle when pressed, notifications that spring open

examples.name: Google Clock / alarm under M3 Expressive
examples.what: the most-shown shape morph: the dial and button shapes change their contour on state change instead of merely swapping color

examples.name: Wear OS 6 (2025)
examples.what: Expressive for round displays - shapes follow the curvature of the case, buttons in groups with responsive width

examples.name: Jetpack Compose androidx.compose.material3
examples.what: MaterialExpressiveTheme, MotionScheme.expressive(), ButtonGroup, FloatingActionButtonMenu - the Expressive APIs are opt-in and marked experimental

examples.name: Material Theme Builder
examples.what: shows the core of the system: one seed hex produces the full tonal scale and from it more than 30 named color roles for light and dark

strengths: The most complete token system in existence - color, shape, type, motion and state are named and machine-readable throughout
Accessibility is built in: color-role pairs guarantee contrast, hit areas are normalized to 48dp
Light and dark are not a second design but two derivations of the same tonal scale
On Android practically free - Compose ships the complete system including spring motion out of the box
Shape morphing is a genuine additional channel of meaning, not just decoration - state stays visible even without color
risks: Outside Android the style reads immediately as 'Android app in a browser' - 28px pills and tonal purple surfaces are Google's brand, not your own
Dynamic Color is the direct antagonist of a brand color: if the user's wallpaper sets the seed, there is no brand color left
The large Expressive shapes are a clear 2025/26 timestamp and will date accordingly
Without a real implementation of state layer, motion and shape morphing, all that remains is 'big radii plus purple' - a caricature of the system
The Expressive APIs in Compose are still experimental and opt-in; on web and desktop the system has to be rebuilt entirely by hand
a11y: Semantic color pairs and generous touch areas provide a useful starting point, not a blanket contrast guarantee. Check the rendered role pairs in every supported mode and state, especially after custom color changes or overlays. This does not require disabling Dynamic Color. The demo uses a fixed palette for a reproducible comparison. Its reduced-motion rule disables morphing and spring movement; a finished product needs that alternative too.
longevity: The token-based core (tonal palettes, color roles, tonal elevation) barely ages and will outlast the next few years. The Expressive surface - very large pills, shape morphing, springy overshoot - is by contrast a clearly datable vintage marker.

platforms.web: Technically easy to rebuild with CSS variables, but alien in design terms - a website in M3 looks like a ported Android client.
platforms.mobile: On Android the native, free and correct choice; on iOS a foreign body against the conventions there.
platforms.desktop: Fits neither macOS nor Windows; in a Tauri window, 56px pills and 28px radii look out of place and waste vertical space.

verdict: As a cross-platform brand: no - M3 is Google's brand, not yours, and anyone who materializes their web and Tauri UI ends up looking like a badly ported Android app. On top of that, Dynamic Color erases exactly the brand color a brand of your own is meant to carry, and the Expressive APIs in Compose are still experimental and opt-in - no foundation for ten years. The right answer is a split one: use M3 on Android, because there it is free, compliant and expected, but with a seed fixed to your own brand color and Dynamic Color switched off. What you should absolutely take over is the method rather than the look: your own tonal scale with fixed tone steps, color roles as pairs, state layers in percent, and a shape scale with three values - that exact scaffolding reproduces identically in Tailwind, Tauri and Compose without anything looking like Google.
tip: NEVER pick a fill color directly, always pick a tone step: surface from tone 90, text on it from tone 10, accent surface from tone 40 with white. And set elevation exclusively through the surface-container steps rather than box-shadow - the moment someone starts stacking shadows on top, M3 tips into arbitrary Flat 2.0 with big radii. If you take only one Expressive ingredient, take the shape morph on press (999px to 12px with a spring curve): it is cheap, it is legible in 200ms, and it carries state even without color.

finder.signature: Every fill is a tone step derived from one seed; the pill morphs into a squircle when pressed.
